Selected engineering work

Evidence over buzzwords.

A selection of real projects, original photographs and engineering workflows. My focus is on the full chain: modelling a system, implementing it, observing its behaviour, diagnosing mismatches and validating the outcome.

01 / MSc dissertation · vehicle control

Adaptive intelligent collision avoidance

Adaptive Intelligent Collision Avoidance System Augmented with Time-to-Collision and Vehicle Stability Constraints. Developed and evaluated a supervisory decision framework that considers collision urgency and vehicle stability when selecting braking, steering or combined interventions. The work focuses on decision logic and control-system validation, rather than claiming a new perception algorithm.

MATLAB / SimulinkStateflowModel Predictive ControlAdaptive TTCVehicle Dynamics
01 / MODEL

Vehicle and risk modelling

Defined relative-motion and time-to-collision logic, with road-friction and stability constraints for intervention decisions.

02 / CONTROL

Supervisory logic

Implemented monitoring, braking, steering and combined response states with Stateflow and model-based control methods.

03 / VALIDATE

Scenario evaluation

Evaluated dry, wet and icy conditions, including higher-fidelity vehicle-dynamics simulation and gated braking responses.

Reported research result: Four out of four final 14-DoF evaluation cases passed the project criteria, with no collisions in those tested cases. This is a simulation result, not a claim of production-vehicle safety certification.
02 / Team lead · end-to-end engineering

Autonomous buggy: from simulation to ground testing

I formed and led the autonomous buggy team, coordinating engineering work from early concepts and simulation through hardware integration, steering/throttle calibration, debugging and controlled vehicle trials. The project brought together software, electronics, actuation and practical verification.

Team leadershipSteering & throttle controldSPACE ControlDeskCalibrationBench & ground tests
01 / PLAN & ORGANISE

Build the team and define the system

Organised the team around the vehicle platform, system interfaces, steering and throttle behaviour, testing tasks and integration priorities.

02 / SIMULATE

Explore control behaviour

Used simulation-oriented workflows to investigate driving behaviour and support safer progression toward physical integration.

03 / INTEGRATE

Connect software and hardware

Worked across control interfaces, actuation, electronics and dSPACE-assisted testing to bring steering and throttle subsystems together.

04 / CALIBRATE

Resolve real actuator mismatches

Investigated left/right steering-response differences, wheel calibration and tuning before proceeding with further trials.

05 / TEST

Bench and controlled ground trials

Planned and conducted staged checks, observed response and repeatability, and used defects to guide refinements.

06 / LEAD & DELIVER

Demonstrate the outcome

Coordinated the team through project delivery and national-level recognition for buggy automation and control-system implementation.

Project summary reflects documented simulation, integration and validation work; quantitative performance figures are not presented without test records.
03 / Autonomous driving · published research

CARLA path planning and driver-in-the-loop simulation

Implemented and compared A* and Dijkstra path-planning approaches in CARLA. Built a multi-screen workflow to inspect routes, vehicle behaviour and Python code, and integrated a Logitech G29 wheel to study interactive steering inputs and simulated vehicle response.

CARLAPythonA* / DijkstraLogitech G29Path following
01 / DEFINE

Route and environment

Defined driving environments and route representations for repeatable autonomous path-planning experiments.

02 / COMPARE

Planning algorithms

Investigated A* and Dijkstra, comparing route-search behaviour and suitability for the simulated scenario.

03 / OBSERVE

Interactive validation

Used route views, driving displays and driver-in-the-loop steering inputs to relate algorithm outputs to vehicle behaviour.

Read the IEEE ISPCC 2025 paper ↗
